questions.q:
The standard reduction potentials at $295K$ for the following half cells are given below:

${NO3}^{-} + 4H^{+} + 3e^{-} \to NO\left(g\right) + 2{H}_{2}O$ $E^{o} = 0 . 97V$
$V^{2 +} \left($aq\right) + 2e^{-} \to V \left($s\right)$ $E^{o} = - 1 . 19V$
${Fe}^{3 +} \left(aq\right) + 3e^{-} \to Fe \left($s\right)$ $E^{o} = - 0 . 04V$
${Ag}^{+} \left(aq\right) + e^{-} \to Ag \left(s\right)$ $E^{o} = 0 . 80V$
${Au}^{3 +} \left(aq\right) + 3e^{-} \to Au \left($s\right)$ $E^{o} = 1 . 40V$

The number of metal(s) which will be oxidised by ${NO3}^{-}$& in aqueous solution is _____.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
For feasibility, check ,& $E^{o}cell = {E}_{cathode ( reduction )}^{o} - {E}_{anode ( oxidation )}^{o} > 0$

The~$E^{o}$~values when metal acts as anode and~${NO}_{3}^{-}$~reaction is cathodic reaction.

For Vanadium metal,~${E}_{cell}^{o} = 0 . 97 + 1 . 19 = 2 . 16V$

For Iron metal,~${E}_{cell}^{o} = 0 . 97 + 0 . 04 = 1 . 01V$

For silver metal,~${E}_{cell}^{o} = 0 . 97 - 0 . 80 = 0 . 17V$

For Gold metal,~${E}_{cell}^{o} = 0 . 97 - 1 . 140 = - 0 . 17V$

For electrodes having oxidation potential greater than $- 0 . 97V$,~$E^{o}cell > 0$

$∴ Ag, Fe$~and~$V$ can be oxidised

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Number of faradays =& $\dfrac{I \times t}{96500}$

~=$\dfrac{2 \times t \times 60 \times 60}{96500}F$

questions.q: $108g$ of silver (molar mass $108g{mol}^{- 1}$ ) is deposited at cathode from ${AgNO}_{3}  \left(aq\right)$ solution by a certain quantity of electricity. The volume (in $L$ ) of oxygen gas produced at $273K$ and $1 bar pressure from water by the same quantity of electricity is ________$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
${\left({n}_{Ag}\right)}_{deposit} = \dfrac{108}{108} = 1mole$
${Ag}^{+} + e^{-} ⟶ Ag$
$1F$ charge is required to deposit $1mole$ of $Ag$
${H}_{2}O⟶ \dfrac{1}{2}{O}_{2} + 2H^{+} + 2e^{-}$
$2F$ charge is required to deposit $\dfrac{1}{2}mole$
$1F$ charge will deposit $\dfrac{1}{4}mole$~of ${O}_{2}$~ gas.
${V}_{{O}_{2}} = \dfrac{nRT}{P}$
$= \dfrac{1}{4} \times \dfrac{0.0821 \times 273}{1} = \dfrac{1}{4} \times 22.4$
${V}_{O2} = 5.6L$

Faraday's second law of electrolysis states that, when the same quantity of electricity is passed through several electrolytes, the mass of the substances deposited are proportional to their respective equivalent weight.

questions.q:
Potassium chlorate is prepared by electrolysis of $KCl$ in basic solution as shown by following equation.

$6{OH}^{-} + {Cl}^{-} \to {ClO}_{3}^{-} + 3{H}_{2}O + 6e^{-}$

A current of $xA$ has to be passed for $10h$ to produce $10 . 0g$ of potassium chlorate. the value of $x$~is __________. (Nearest integer)

(Molar mass of ${KClO}_{3} = 122 . 6g{mol}^{- 1}F = 96500C$)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Given balanced equation is

$\overset{⊝}{60H} + \overset{⊝}{C}l ⟶ {ClO}_{3}^{-} + 3{H}_{2}O + 6e^{-}$

$\to 10{gKClO}_{3} ⇒ \dfrac{10}{122 . 6}{molKCO}_{3}$~in obtained

→ from the above reaction, it is concluded that by
$6F$ charge $1{molKClO}_{3}$ is obtained.

→ By the passage of $6F$ charge $= 1{molKClO}_{3}$

$∴$ By the passage of $\dfrac{x \times 10 \times 60 \times 60}{96500}F$~charge

$= \dfrac{1}{6} \times \dfrac{x \times 10 \times 60 \times 60}{96500}$

Now~$\dfrac{x \times 10 \times 60 \times 60}{6 \times 96500} = \dfrac{10}{122 . 6}$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{10 \times 965}{60 \times 122 . 6} = \dfrac{965}{735 . 6} = 1 . 311 ≃ 1$

OR

$W = \dfrac{E}{F} \times I \times t$

$10 = \dfrac{122 . 6}{96500 \times 6} \times x \times 10 \times 3600$

$X = 1 . 311$

questions.solution:
Cell reaction is:

$\text{Sn} ( \text{s} ) + {\text{Pb}}^{+ 2} ( \text{aq} ) \to {\text{Sn}}^{+ 2} ( \text{aq} ) + \text{Pb} ( \text{s} )$

Apply Nernst equation:

${E}_{\text{cell}} = {E}_{\text{cell}}^{0} - \dfrac{0.06}{2} log\dfrac{ \left[{\text{Sn}}^{+ 2}\right]}{ \left[{\text{Pb}}^{+ 2}\right]} ..... \left($1\right)$

{E}_{\text{cell}}^{0} = - 0.13 + 0.14 = 0.$01\text{V}

At equilibrium : \text{E}\text{cell} =$0$ Substituting in (1)

$0 = 0.01 - $\dfrac{0.0$0$06}{2}log\dfrac{ \left[{\text{Sn}}^{+ 2}\right]}{\left[{\text{Pb}}^{+ 2}\right]}

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{3} ==log\dfrac{\left[{\text{Sn}}^{+ 2}\right]}{\left[{\text{Pb}}^{+ 2}\right]}

$⇒ $\dfrac{\left[{\text{Sn}}^{+ 2}\right]}{\left[{\text{Pb}}^{+ 2}\right]} =$2.15$

\left[{Cu}^{2 +}\right] = \dfrac{Ksp}{\left[{OH}^{-}\right]2} = \dfrac{1 .0 \times {10}^{- 20}M^{2}}{1M} =$1 .0 $\times {10}^{- 20}$M$

~ ~ ~ $E =0.34 V - $\$left(\dfrac{0 .059 V}{2}\rrright)log\dfrac{1}{1 .0 \times {10}^{- 20}} =0 .34 V - \dfrac{0 .059 \times 20V}{2}E = 0 . 34 - 0 . 59 = - 0 . 25V$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
For given cell reaction $n = 2$
and $\Delta G ° = - nFE ° , cell \Delta G ° = \Delta H ° - T \Delta S$
Then $\Delta H ° = 825 . 2 \times {10}^{3}J / mole$
$T = 298K$
$E{°}_{cell} = 4 . 315V$
$F = 96487C$
$\Delta S ° = \dfrac{- \left(- nFE{°}_{cell} - \Delta H\right)}{T}$
$\Delta S ° = \dfrac{- \left(- 2 \times 96487 \times 4 . 315 - \left(- 825 . 2 \times {10}^{3}\right)\right)}{298} = \dfrac{832 . 682 \times {10}^{3} - 825 . 2 \times {10}^{3}}{298} = \dfrac{7482}{298} \times {10}^{3}$
$\Delta S ° = 25 . 1J / k$
